newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: More war if Kabila tries for total power, Modise.
newsitem.headline: More war if Kabila tries for total power, Modise.

text.p: South African Defence Minister Joe Modise on Friday predicted continuing war in Zaire if rebel leader Laurent Kabila spurned other groups and tried to take all power for his own alliance.
Modise told reporters South Africa was trying to dissuade Kabila from his insistence that President Mobutu Sese Seko hand power to his alliance, rather than to a broad-based transitional authority.
"We believe it's in the interest of Kabila himself," said Modise, who has been closely involved in South Africa's efforts to avoid a bloody battle for Kinshasa.

"Kabila's men are poised at the gates of Kinshasa and he's threatening now to strike at Kinshasa," Modise said. "We believe if he goes that route, it's going to create lots of problems for him in future."
He said there was goodwill towards Kabila among many of the people and political parties based in Kinshasa.

"It's in his interest to take them on board. To smash Kinshasa now, the people and those parties, will have repercussions which will live with him for a long time to come and it will make his ascension to power very unstable."
Asked if this meant the civil war would go on, Modise replied: "This is our fear."
He said South Africa was determined to bring a peaceful resolution to the conflict partly out of self-interest, because turmoil in Zaire would send a flood of refugees to the south.
"A small hiccup in Zaire, there are planeloads of people coming here. You can imagine when Kinshasa and Gbadolite are being attacked, what is going to happen -- we'll have another exodus.
"Even if they go to Angola, they're going to end up here. Those who are going to Zambia, are going to end up here. Our country is already overflowing with refugees," Modise said.
